question: Which of the following best describes doping in semiconductors?
options: Doping changes silicon into a metal.
Doping adds charge carriers that control conductivity.
Doping makes semiconductors into perfect insulators.
Pure silicon conducts better than doped silicon.
gold_answer: Doping adds charge carriers that control conductivity.
notes: Team-authored original item on doping in semiconductors. Passages are team-authored derivations recorded under sciclaim-appx-A. Requires independent annotation and adjudication before any gate result is reported.

positions.answer: Doping makes semiconductors into perfect insulators.

evidence.text: Phosphorus atoms in silicon each bring a fifth valence electron that is free to conduct.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes a free conducting electron per donor, which entails the claim.

claims.text: More doping always improves transistor performance.

evidence.text: Beyond an optimum, heavy doping increases scattering and leakage, harming performance.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states heavy doping harms performance, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Silicon works for all electronic applications.

evidence.text: Material choices were surveyed across the device catalogue.

claims.verdict_rationale: A survey cannot show one material fits all uses, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Pure silicon conducts better than doped silicon.

evidence.text: Boron atoms lack one bond electron, leaving holes that move as positive carriers.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes mobile holes from acceptors, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Doped regions contain no electric fields.

evidence.text: Charge separation at junctions builds in strong local fields that govern device action.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states strong local fields exist, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Quantum computers already outperform all classical ones.

evidence.text: Benchmark scores were reported for one quantum and one classical processor.

claims.verdict_rationale: One comparison cannot show universal superiority, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Doping changes silicon into a metal.

claims.text: A p-n junction rectifies current flow.

evidence.text: The junction passes current easily one way while blocking the reverse direction.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes one-way conduction, which entails the claim.

evidence.text: Excess heat creates runaway carriers and degrades junctions, so devices need thermal limits.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states heat degrades devices, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Smaller transistors are always better in every respect.

evidence.text: Speed and leakage were measured across three process nodes.

claims.verdict_rationale: Three nodes cannot show always better in every respect, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.
